title: Accessibility of derived local equivalences in a combinatorial model category
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the model-category, locally presentable and combinatorial terminology of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial model category with functorial factorizations, and let $S$ be a small set of its arrows. Use the original homotopy function complexes $\operatorname{Map}^h$ of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping]. Call an originally fibrant object $Z$ local if $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$. Let $W_S$ be the full subcategory of the ordinary arrow category $\mathcal M^{[1]}$ whose objects are those $f:X\to Y$ for which $\operatorname{Map}^h(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z)$ is an equivalence for every such local $Z$; morphisms in the arrow category are commuting squares. Then $W_S$ is replete, accessible, and accessibly embedded: for some infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal M^{[1]}$ and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Replete means closed under isomorphisms in the arrow category. Here $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means that a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of size less than $\lambda$ has size less than $\lambda$. No left properness or simplicial enrichment is assumed, and the endpoints of the arrows of $S$ need not be cofibrant.

source.place: Barwick, Lemma 4.6, using Lemma 4.5, printed p. 43. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Write $W_0$ for the original weak equivalences and $\mathcal Z$ for the originally fibrant $S$-local objects. By [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], the specified $\operatorname{Map}^h$ is the mapping space in the original homotopy coherent localization, so every arrow of $W_0$ induces equivalences on these spaces. Thus $W_0\subseteq W_S$. The mapping-space definition shows two-out-of-three for $W_S$ by applying $\operatorname{Map}^h(-,Z)$ for each $Z\in\mathcal Z$. An isomorphism of arrows conjugates each tested map by equivalences, proving repleteness.

source.place: Definition 4.1 and Lemma 4.6: original derived mapping-space test.

proof.text: Choose a small original generating set $I$ of cofibrations. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] to $I$ and $\varnothing\to X$, obtaining a functor $Q$ and a natural trivial fibration $q_X:QX\to X$ with $QX$ cofibrant. The right lifting class of $I$ is the original trivial fibrations by combinatoriality. Original cofibrations form the left lifting class against these maps; [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] show that this class is weakly saturated, so the left factor is an original cofibration. The middle-object functor is accessible. For a nonempty filtered category, its constant initial diagram has initial colimit: a cocone into any object is unique. Since arrow colimits are computed at endpoints, $X\mapsto(\varnothing\to X)$ preserves filtered colimits. Hence $Q$ is accessible. Naturality gives $q_YQf=fq_X$; step 1 and two-out-of-three yield $f\in W_S\Longleftrightarrow Qf\in W_S$.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, accessible replacement input expanded using HTT Proposition A.1.2.5.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-framed-localizing-cofibrations] to the original model category and the small set $S$, obtaining $H$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] to $H$ and $QX\to1$. Let $RX$ be the middle object and $a_X:QX\to RX$ the left factor. The right factor $RX\to1$ has all $H$-lifts, so $RX\in\mathcal Z$. The map $a_X$ lies in the weak saturation of $H$ and its source $QX$ is cofibrant; the second clause of the framing node therefore gives $a_X\in W_S$. Since all of $H$ are original cofibrations, [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] show that their weak saturation consists of original cofibrations. Thus $a_X$ is a cofibration, and composing it with the initial cofibration of $QX$ shows that $RX$ is cofibrant. No assertion about cellular maps with arbitrary noncofibrant source is used.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, accessible local replacement expanded using the framed lifting-test prerequisite; Hirschhorn Definition 3.3.8, Lemma 3.3.11, Theorem 17.8.4, Proposition 17.8.8, Corollary 17.8.12 and Proposition 17.8.14, without the properness assumptions of Section 4.2.

proof.text: Functoriality of the second factorization gives $R$ and a natural transformation $a:Q\to R$, in particular $Rf\,a_X=a_YQf$. Its middle-object functor preserves sufficiently filtered colimits. The functor $QX\mapsto(QX\to1)$ does also: filtered indices are nonempty and connected, and cocones from their constant terminal diagram to $T$ are exactly maps $1\to T$, so its colimit is $1$. Choose a regular cardinal at least the two accessibility cardinals (the larger of two regular cardinals); filteredness at it implies filteredness at each smaller one. Thus the composite $R$ is accessible. Two-out-of-three applied to the displayed naturality square and $a_X,a_Y\in W_S$ gives $Qf\in W_S\Longleftrightarrow Rf\in W_S$. Combined with step 2, $f\in W_S\Longleftrightarrow Rf\in W_S$.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, constructive accessible local replacement; functoriality and filtered-colimit comparison written out.

proof.text: Let $u:U\to V$ be an arrow between objects of $\mathcal Z$. The mapping spaces of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] have component sets equal to morphisms in $h\mathcal M_\infty$: a component identifies edges exactly by homotopies, which is the definition of $h$ in [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category]. That node identifies $h\mathcal M_\infty$ with the ordinary localization. If $u\in W_S$, test against $U$ and $V$. Surjectivity of $u^*:[V,U]\to[U,U]$ supplies $g$ with $gu=1_U$. Injectivity of $u^*:[V,V]\to[U,V]$ and $(ug)u=u=1_Vu$ give $ug=1_V$. Therefore $u$ is invertible in the original ordinary localization, and [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] gives $u\in W_0$. Conversely $W_0\subseteq W_S$ by step 1. Since $RX,RY\in\mathcal Z$, this proves the decisive equivalence $f\in W_S\Longleftrightarrow Rf\in W_0$.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, omitted accessibility inference: explicit inverse in the original homotopy category.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-model-weak-equivalences-accessible], the full original weak-equivalence subcategory $W_0\subseteq\mathcal M^{[1]}$ is replete, accessible and accessibly embedded. Its hypothesis is precisely combinatoriality of the original model structure. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-arrow-inverse-image] to $R:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$: both underlying categories are locally presentable by the item hypothesis, $R$ is accessible by step 4, and $W_0$ satisfies its subcategory hypothesis. The inverse image is exactly $W_S$ by step 5. The conclusion supplies a regular cardinal $\lambda$ for which $W_S$ is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered arrow colimits and generated under those colimits by a small set. Together with step 1 this is every clause of the item, including ambient accessibly embeddedness.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, accessibility conclusion, made explicit by existing generic inverse-image theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q125-e5e2c5e7f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full; review.md has the details. Neither source is in literature/, so I fetched both read-only and checked them at the cited places. Item: the statement is unchanged and matches Barwick Def. 4.2.2-4.2.3 and Lemma 4.6 (printed p. 43). That lemma assumes only a combinatorial M and a small H; left properness enters only at Theorem 4.7. Barwick's proof shows closure under filtered colimits and only asserts accessibility; the delivery proves it constructively. Steps: in step 2, the left factor from I is a cofibration by lifting-class-closure and transfinite-left-lifting, the right factor is a trivial fibration, and functoriality gives q_Y Qf = f q_X. In step 3, the H-injective middle object is fibrant and local, and a_X is a local equivalence by clause 2 because its source QX is cofibrant. Step 4 composes accessible functors. In step 5, Yoneda on pi_0 in hM_inf (the ordinary localization) gives gu=1 and ug=1, and the detection lemma gives u in W_0. In step 6, the arrow inverse image of the accessible class W_0 under the accessible R is W_S. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. New node lem-cbc-framed-localizing-cofibrations: true for H = horns plus J (Hirschhorn Def. 4.2.1-4.2.2). Clause 1 follows from Lemma 3.3.11, which holds in any model category; Prop. 4.2.4 sits under a left-proper heading, but its proof does not use it. Clause 2 follows from Prop. 17.8.14(1), Prop. 17.8.11, Cor. 17.8.12(1), Props. 17.8.13 and 17.8.7, and the tower argument in Thm. 17.8.18. The cofibrant-source restriction is needed and kept, and a retract under U is obtained by factoring the map itself. Small cases (S empty, terminal M, S={0->1}, the n=0 horn) are consistent. The node is statement-only, self-contained TeX with three kinds of logged searches and correct created/blueprint fields. It neither restates a clause of the item nor duplicates general-bousfield-localization, simplicial-bousfield-model-structure, cofibration-local-mapping-test, left-proper-derived-cell-colimits, bousfield-local-fibrations or cosimplicial-frame-mapping. I accept the six declared tool_uses (generic sk-prop-sf-biduality-general infrastructure, the same family accepted for the parent). No SGA is cited, no target, unit or chapter is touched, and I wrote no fixes.

lean.note: The three helper predicates render the notions introduced in this node. Derived precomposition uses the canonical source-evaluation leg from maps in Fun([1],K) from q(f) to id(qZ); its target-evaluation leg is canonically an equivalence to Map(qY,qZ). This is the evaluation span of FrameMappingRelation, without a simplicial enrichment hypothesis or a chosen replacement map. The conclusion spells out precisely repleteness, ambient filtered-colimit closure and small generation, as in the recorded accessibility prerequisites.
